marker_line: Fortio workflows: unchanged CI config fetch; fix dotfile false positives
decisive_evidence: forager recovered the original GitHub main archive byte-for-byte at the supplied SHA-256. Its tree exactly matches upstream e76cb112.

Fetched v0.1.0-pre7 (f548989ad1a1c17000c36c9e92e237f94db53ffe, 2024-07-15). Both workflows already download the same config URLs to .goreleaser.yaml and .golangci.yml. The release command itself is byte-identical.
Compared immediate predecessor 9adc1753cd629f9edfc976e11f55d96813a8f549: only three CodeQL action SHA pins change. No new download, command, endpoint or credential use.

Changes since pre7 update action/toolchain versions, add cross-platform lint/test coverage, and parameterize main package, binary and Dockerfile names. GoReleaser config remains release packaging for Fortio Docker images and homebrew-tap.
Earlier release and predecessor both trigger these two suspicious rules under current rules; the queue claim of an earlier clean scan is not reproducible with the recovered versions.
execution_trace: Tag/reusable release job checks out source, configures QEMU/buildx, and passes explicitly supplied Docker credentials to Docker login. It installs Go and curls the project shared release config. The GoReleaser action is tag-gated and receives GH_PAT as GITHUB_TOKEN for publishing, plus explicit build parameters.

Downloaded config builds the caller Go main for Linux/Windows/Darwin amd64/arm64 with CGO disabled, generates checksums and archives, publishes Fortio container images/manifests and Homebrew formulas. Homebrew test invokes the packaged binary with -version. No unexpected external hook or shell payload is configured.

gochecks installs and runs upstream govulncheck, downloads shared golangci-lint settings on Ubuntu, runs pinned lint action, then runs go buildinfo and either make test or go test -race. The YAML settings select analyzers/formatters and exclusions, with no plugin or executable payload.

Coverage runs make coverage or go test -coverprofile, then passes CODECOV_TOKEN to the configured Codecov action. CodeQL performs Go init/autobuild/analyze. Secrets are used in their intended action inputs/environments, with no source-to-unrelated-send chain.

newrepo.sh is an interactive repository provisioning utility: prompts for name/description, creates a public Fortio repo from its template, substitutes placeholders in tracked files, copies a website entry, runs go mod tidy/go run, commits/pushes, and sets branch rules and repository options via gh api. These declared administrative effects fit its purpose.

Archive members are readable source/configuration. There is no obfuscated stage to decode. cleave facts was run on original, releaser manifest, and every extracted shell run block; decoded strings contain no additional payload. No sample commands were executed.
limitations: Downstream caller source, caller secret values, mutable main/latest references, external actions and future HTTP responses are runtime inputs. The verdict concerns these collected bytes, not an invented deployment or all future resolutions.

The engine marks gochecks.yml and releaser.yml embedded-source-incomplete and omits some conditional shell steps. Every run block was manually extracted and analyzed as shell to inspect those paths. No YAML rule can repair that producer omission.
changes: Narrowed the existing hidden-output and relative-dotfile observations for exact root output names .goreleaser.yml/.yaml and .golangci.yml/.yaml. These are documented conventional configuration names: the unsupported inference was concealment/security-boundary crossing from their leading dot alone.

Exclusions target output arguments, not arbitrary URL mentions, path substrings or whole files. Temporary hidden files, suffix variants and other hidden downloads in a mixed file retain detection. Existing curl/network/output observations stay notable.
No traits renamed, moved or severity-reduced; no blanket project or CI allowlist added.

shell-curl-hidden-output feeds objectives/command-and-control/dropper/delivery/hidden-stage::hidden-download-shell-execution. The existing gha-dunelinebyte-artifact-tamper-linux.tgz fixture retains its hostile composite and suspicious atom in container, action manifest and embedded run block.

Existing model-backdoor-hidden-relative-download.sh, model-backdoor-loader.sh and benign github-actions-download-execution-controls/action.yml retain exactly all original IDs and criticalities before/after. The benign fixture preserves accurate dual-use hidden-download behavior.
